reviews.reasoning: Re-derived from the witnesses, not from the row. Listen to my prayer.” web:Ps.61.1) — argued from the pointed bytes plus both renderings, since the staged extract carries no morphology layer. 2 of 2 pointed Hebrew runs in this row collate at byte tier; 4 of 4 curly-quoted WEB spans are verbatim against their own cited ref with no neighbour slack. reviews.reasoning: Everything load-bearing here re-derives correctly. Span web:Ps.61.5-Ps.61.8 = oshb:Ps.61.6-Ps.61.9; the prose dual-cites and all 4 boundary_evidence_refs pairs in the row satisfy ps_lib.web_to_mt exactly (citation_sweep.py: 0 problems). 5 of 5 pointed Hebrew runs collate at byte tier against their cited refs, including (web:Ps.61.6 = oshb:Ps.61.7) יָמִ֣ים עַל יְמֵי מֶ֣לֶךְ, whose maqaf-free serialisation matches the staged extract (0 x U+05BE book-wide) — the row asserts no maqaf. 4 of 4 curly-quoted WEB spans are verbatim against their own ref with no neighbour slack. The vow bracket is real at both ends, (web:Ps.61.5 = oshb:Ps.61.6) לִנְדָרָ֑י and (web:Ps.61.8 = oshb:Ps.61.9) לְֽשַׁלְּמִ֥י נְדָרַ֗י, skeleton sweep נדרי: 2 verses in Ps 61 — a genuine tier-1 warrant for holding web:Ps.61.5 with the royal material instead of with the preceding refuge strophe, which is exactly the seam the row defends. The Elohistic figure checks out: psalm_device_inventory.json yhwh_elohim_per_psalm for 61 is yhwh 0 / elohim 3, re-derived from bytes as unsuffixed אלהים at oshb:Ps.61.2, oshb:Ps.61.6, oshb:Ps.61.8 (= web:Ps.61.1, web:Ps.61.5, web:Ps.61.7; 3 tokens in 3 verses, 0 inseparable-prefixed forms in this psalm), and the Book II 32/165 comparison matches the inventory line. Confidence medium is if anything conservative for a seam carrying selah corroboration, a grounding clause and a lexical bracket. Two sub-material observations, filed as observations because neither contests span, warrant or fact: (1) check_web_quotes.py flags the curly quote ‘the king’ in observed_substrate_signals[0] as carrying no web: ref in its own field — the string is genuine WEB wording (web:Ps.61.6 reads “You will prolong the king's life.”), so this is a missing inline ref, not a gloss dressed as a quotation; (2) check_universals.py flags ‘carries no Yahweh’ in device_notes as a universal with no adjacent digit-bearing sweep — the claim is right but ships no digit for the zero.

The envelope reading survives re-derivation, and one of the row's collate claims is exactly right. The opening and returning lines are related but not repeated: collate of the full oshb:Ps.62.2 (= web:Ps.62.1) against the full oshb:Ps.62.6 (= web:Ps.62.5) returns tier none, and the substitutions the row names are byte-true. The refrain observation also holds: collate with quote = oshb:Ps.62.7 (= web:Ps.62.6) against window oshb:Ps.62.3 (= web:Ps.62.2) returns skeleton tier, 3 of 3 opening words are identical at byte tier, and oshb:Ps.62.3 carries the extra closing רַבָּֽה that oshb:Ps.62.7 lacks — so the span ends on the second refrain line, a defensible refrain-lattice close (the shared seam at web:Ps.62.6|62.7 is contested at the adjoining row, where the warrant for it lives). 9 of 9 pointed Hebrew runs collate at byte tier. The selah handling is honest in principle (disclosed as mid-row, explicitly not the driver) but misnumbered in fact (pmarks_Ps.json records 2 selah verses in Ps 62): the earlier of them is at oshb:Ps.62.5 = web:Ps.62.4, not at the oshb:Ps.62.6 the signal names, and oshb:Ps.62.6 carries no selah in the inventory. Five evidence defects follow, one of them a wrong WEB reading carrying the envelope's closing member; confidence high is not supportable while the return line is documented from the wrong verse.
